clue.text: Old lecturer enters competition with authority

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it goes inside it

parts.note: a race is a competition

explanation.surface: An elderly academic signs up for a contest and speaks with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts L inside RACE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person or source whose word is taken as authoritative, so an authority.

clue.text: Turkish delight at last — after starter of olives, am not upset!

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so this takes the opening letter of olives
this takes only the final letter of the word delight
upset means knocked over or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to be put out after a nibble of olives at a meal of Turkish delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkish delight' looks like one phrase, but Turkish is the definition. 'upset' rearranges AM NOT into TOMAN, after O and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman describes the Turkish empire and its people, so it is a synonym of Turkish.

clue.text: Spy gets kind of crimson once cover's blown

indicators.note: with its cover gone, the word loses its outer letters at each end

parts.note: magenta is a purplish-crimson colour

explanation.surface: A spy is rattled when an undercover identity is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once cover's blown' strips the outer M and A from MAGENTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone who works secretly for an intelligence service, a spy.

clue.text: Singer Moyet left first to hide one love affair

indicators.note: hiding something means putting it inside, so one letter goes within the rest
the letter for left is moved to the front of the singer's name

parts.note: Alison Moyet is an English pop singer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Alison Moyet leaves early to keep a romance secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' moves the L of ALISON to the front, giving LAISON; 'to hide' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship.

clue.text: Joker breaks into school for change

indicators.note: one piece breaking into another goes inside it

parts.note: a wit is a clever joker

explanation.surface: A prankster breaks into a school to swap something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' suggests a playing card or a comedian, but here it means a witty person.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap one thing for another, a change.

clue.text: Line in what you're reading to classes

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: the reader is reading words right now

explanation.surface: A line in the text you are reading out to classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside WORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Worlds can mean distinct spheres or groups, as in the world of fashion, so classes or categories.

clue.text: Lift prize cup of the highest quality

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting means the letters read upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is a cup awarded as a trophy

explanation.surface: Winning the trophy and holding it up marks a first-class achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reverses REWARDPOT, reading upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for things of the finest class, the best quality.

clue.text: Listen to the end of our bust-up in anger

indicators.note: one piece in another goes inside it

parts.note: heat is a sense of anger or passion

indicators.note: a bust-up breaks things apart, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Hearing out the end of a furious quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen to the end' is the definition, not a pointer to final letters; 'bust-up' scrambles our, and 'in' places it within heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear someone out is to let them finish speaking, listening until they are done.

clue.text: Second chicken drinks beer on top of barn for encouragement …

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, a second

indicators.note: something that drinks takes it in, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a rooster is a male chicken
ale is beer

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter in a down answer

explanation.surface: A cockerel briefly downing beer on a barn roof, as a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes the first letter of barn, and 'drinks' puts that and the beer inside the chicken. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A morale booster is something that lifts spirits, a source of encouragement.

clue.text: Egypt is regularly overturning complaint

indicators.note: turning over means the letters are read backwards
taking letters at regular intervals means every other one from the words Egypt is

explanation.surface: Egypt keeps overturning a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes EYTS from EGYPTIS; 'overturning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a medical complaint.

clue.text: A fake prophecy: 'Earth's lost metal' — it's doubtful

indicators.note: fake means made up, so these letters are reworked
something lost is gone from the word, so the letter is removed

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
AL is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a metal

explanation.surface: A bogus prediction of the Earth losing its metal is dubious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes E out of PROPHECY; 'fake' rearranges PROPHCY into POCRYPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocryphal describes a story of questionable authenticity, widely told but probably untrue.

clue.text: Text about new hit fashions

indicators.note: one piece about another goes around it

parts.note: SMS is a text message

indicators.note: making something new means reworking it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A text message about a new hit in the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashions' looks like a noun about clothes, but it is a verb: shapes or forges. 'new' scrambles hit and 'about' wraps the text around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To smith is to forge or shape metal, so smiths is a verb meaning crafts or shapes.

clue.text: English bowler moves around leg — wicket falls!

indicators.note: a wicket that falls is lost, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to wander is to move around
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
ON is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: An England bowler shifts around the leg side and takes a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' removes W from WANDERSON. In cricket, the leg side is also called the on side. James Anderson is England's record Test wicket-taker.
explanation.definitionFit: James Anderson is a celebrated English fast bowler in cricket.

clue.text: Is footballer blocking Everton's last delivery?

indicators.note: a letter blocked in sits inside the word around it
the final letter of the team name Everton

parts.note: a winger is a footballer playing on the flank

explanation.surface: Whether a footballer can block an Everton player's final delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts N, the last of Everton, inside IS. Everton is an English football club; an inswinger is a ball curving inward in cricket or football.
explanation.definitionFit: An inswinger is a bowled or kicked ball that curves inwards, a type of delivery.

clue.text: … as Goldberg and sheep celebrate raucously

parts.note: Whoopi Goldberg is an American actress
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Whoopi Goldberg and a flock of sheep partying loudly together.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from the previous clue's 'encouragement'.
explanation.definitionFit: To whoop it up is an idiom for having a loud, lively party.

clue.text: Drunk hides whiskey in study

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drunk stashes whisky in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' puts W inside SOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To swot is British slang for studying hard, especially for exams.

clue.text: Following kick-off, running back for corner

indicators.note: running back means the letters are read in reverse
one piece following another comes after it

parts.note: a machine that is on is running

explanation.surface: After kick-off a player runs back to take a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places running after kick-off, and 'back' reverses the whole; the football surface hides that corner simply means a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or sheltered corner of a room.

clue.text: Ozone damaged, I see, by this age

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C sounds like see, a standard crossword letter

explanation.surface: Ozone damage in the present era, as I can see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges OZONE into NEOZO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neozoic is an old geological name for the most recent era, the present age of the Earth.

clue.text: Work in bed? Initially, employer to play along

indicators.note: one piece in another goes inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
an opera is a musical work

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word employer

explanation.surface: Is working in bed allowed? The boss decides whether to go along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a musical work here, not a job; 'in' places it within the bed, and 'Initially' takes the first letter of employer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work along with others, to go along willingly.

clue.text: Pepper pot shaken over fried carbon-free mince

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
fried food is cooked up into something new, another rearranging signal
free of carbon means the chemical symbol for carbon is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe step: shake a pot of pepper over fried mince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon-free' removes C from MINCE; 'fried' and 'shaken' jumble POT and MINE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is a sweet red pepper, also called pimiento, used in stuffing olives.

clue.text: Cambridge college's uprising — can I go outside?

indicators.note: one piece outside another goes around it

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A student revolt at Cambridge: may I leave?
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses TINI into INIT; 'outside' puts TRY around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity College is one of the largest colleges of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Unscramble what Enigma produced?

definitions.meaning: to unscramble a coded message is to turn it back into plain text
an Enigma machine at the receiving end turned ciphertext back into readable German

explanation.surface: Cracking the output of the wartime cipher machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigma was the German cipher machine of the Second World War; the same machine, set up identically, both scrambled and unscrambled messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher a coded message is to turn its scrambled text back into plain language.

clue.text: Animated figure's bearing American god

parts.note: Morph is a plasticine character in British children's television animation
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A cartoon character carries itself like an American deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Morph is a small clay figure from British children's TV programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpheus is the Greek god of dreams and sleep.

clue.text: In speech ex-PM beguiles table

indicators.note: in speech means the letters entered sound like the phrase spoken

parts.note: Theresa May is a former Prime Minister; to beguile someone is to trick them

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister charms the House with a table of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular grid of numbers or data, a kind of table.

clue.text: Cheers when husband quits and fails badly

indicators.note: something that quits leaves, so its letter is taken out

parts.note: cheers is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A toast goes sour when the husband walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' removes H from THANKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks is informal for flops or collapses, as a show or share price fails dramatically.

clue.text: Perhaps email in the latest style?

definitions.meaning: email is a modern kind of post, so the answer split in two describes it
... names the art movement after modernism, cheekily read as later than modern

explanation.surface: Is email just letters written in the newest fashion?
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the answer reads as modern post, which email is; whole, it is the style that followed modernism.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmodern names the style after modernism, which sounds like the latest, and email is modern mail.

clue.text: Type of film only showing in visible and ultraviolet light?

definitions.text: Type of film only showing in visible and ultraviolet light?

parts.words: Type of film only showing in visible and ultraviolet light?
parts.note: a film shown with no infrared, abbreviated IR

explanation.surface: A movie that can only be screened under ordinary and UV lights.
explanation.walkthrough: Light that is only visible and ultraviolet has no infrared, IR in science shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Noir, as in film noir, is a dark, cynical genre of crime cinema.

clue.text: Fancy pheromone contains secret message

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them across the word break

explanation.surface: An elaborate scent chemical carries a coded signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' signals the answer lies across 'Fancy pheromone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypher, also spelt cipher, is a coded or secret message.

clue.text: Timid setter's crossing river

indicators.note: one piece crossing another spans it, so the outer letters go around

parts.note: the setter's means my, from the setter's point of view
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A shy crossword setter wades across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' wraps the setter's word around the river; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousey describes someone shy and quiet, like a timid little mouse.
